source_observations: AppHandle::plugin_boxed acquires manager.plugins, then calls PluginStore::initialize before releasing the mutex.
PluginStore::initialize invokes TauriPlugin::initialize, whose setup callback is user code and receives an AppHandle.
AppHandle::plugin and AppHandle::remove_plugin acquire the same manager.plugins mutex.
AppManager::run_plugin_invoke_handler holds manager.plugins while calling the selected plugin's extend_api/invoke handler.
on_event_loop_event holds manager.plugins while invoking PluginStore::on_event, which calls plugin lifecycle hooks.
consequence: A plugin setup, invoke handler, or lifecycle hook that performs a nested dynamic plugin register/remove operation can try to reacquire the same non-reentrant std::sync::Mutex on the same thread and block indefinitely.
prepared_probe: The retained setup probe uses try_lock inside a plugin setup callback instead of recursively calling plugin(), so it can establish whether the public callback is entered while the plugin-store mutex is held without hanging the test process.
limitations: Probe has not been executed against the pinned target in a retained target receipt.
A repair must preserve plugin registration ordering and same-name replacement semantics; simply dropping the store lock before initialization may introduce concurrent initialization races.
Invoke-handler and lifecycle-hook reentrancy need separate controls because their ownership/borrowing path differs from dynamic setup.
